items.title: A birational morphism between schemes with finitely many components is an isomorphism over the local ring of a generic point of the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a birational morphism between schemes with finitely many irreducible components, the base change to the local ring at a generic point of the target is an isomorphism (statement lines 13236-13243). The counted proof is a short but genuine commutative algebra reduction: it passes to an affine irreducible situation, identifies the generic point with a minimal prime, uses birationality to know that the corresponding local rings are isomorphic and that there is a unique minimal prime upstairs, and then shows that the localized source ring has exactly one prime by exhibiting the extension of the minimal prime as both minimal and maximal, from which the identification with the base change follows (proof lines 13245-13260). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard dictionary between points, minimal primes and local rings.
